questions.question: State the rule for chairs around a row of n tables in words and in symbols, and justify each part.
questions.expected_answer: Two chairs per table plus two end chairs: c = 2n + 2. Each table has a chair on its top and bottom side (2n), and the row has one chair at each end (+2).

questions.question: Show that 2(n + 1) and 2n + 2 are equivalent, and explain what each describes.
questions.expected_answer: Expanding 2(n + 1) gives 2n + 2. The first imagines an extra table and gives every table two chairs; the second counts two per table and two at the ends. Same chairs, different counting.

questions.question: Why is 4n wrong for the number of dots on the border of an n-by-n grid, and what is the correct rule?
questions.expected_answer: Each corner dot lies on two sides and is counted twice by 4n; for n = 3, 4n gives 12 but there are 8. Subtracting the four double-counted corners gives 4n − 4.
